'''Matt Davison''' is a Canadian mathematician and university professor. He is a currently serving as Professor at the Departments of Statistical & Actuarial Science<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty |url=http://www.uwo.ca/stats/people/faculty.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> and Mathematics,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full-Time Faculty |url=http://www.math.uwo.ca/faculty/index.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.math.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> Dean of the Faculty of Science<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dean's Office Staff |url=http://www.uwo.ca/sci/about_science/people.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> at [[Western University (Canada)|Western University]]. Davison is also the Director of Canada's Financial Wellness lab.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Matt Davison {{!}} Canada's Financial Wellness Lab |url=https://www.financialwellnesslab.ca/matt-davison |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Canada's FWL |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
After graduating from the [[University of Toronto]] with a Bachelor of Applied Science in Engineering Science (1991), Davison attended [[Western University (Canada)|Western University]] where he earned a M.Sc (1993) and Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics (1995).

== Career and work ==
Before entering academia, Davison worked as Assistant Vice President of Equity Arbitrage at [[Deutsche Bank]] Canada from 1997 to 1999.<ref name=":1" /> Prior to this role, he was a [[postdoctoral research fellow]] at the Physiology Institute of the [[University of Bern]], Switzerland, from 1995 to 1997.<ref name=":1" />

Since joining Western University in 1999,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dean's Biography |url=http://www.uwo.ca/sci/about_science/deans_message/biography.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> Davison has focused his research in the field of [[quantitative finance]]. His significant contributions to the field include authoring ''Quantitative Finance: A Simulation-Based Introduction Using Excel in 2014'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Davison |first=Matt |title=Quantitative Finance: A Simulation-Based Introduction Using Excel |publisher=[[CRC Press]] |year=2014 |isbn=978-1439871683 |publication-date=May 8, 2014}}</ref> 9 book chapters, and publishing over 80 papers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matt Davison |url=https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=pEdDqE0AAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=scholar.google.ca}}</ref> Davison has 23 PhD students graduated from his research group, and 4 PhD students in current progress.<ref name=":1" />

Davison held a Tier 2 [[Canada Research Chair]] in [[Quantitative finance|Quantitative Finance]] from 2006 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/transparency-transparence/disclosure-divulgation/grants-subventions/2006.pdf
| title = Grants and Subventions 2006
| publisher = Canada Research Chairs
| format = PDF
| access-date = 2024-06-12
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/transparency-transparence/disclosure-divulgation/grants-subventions/2011.pdf
| title = Grants and Subventions 2011
| publisher = Canada Research Chairs
| format = PDF
| access-date = 2024-06-12
}}
</ref> In 2015, he was named a [[Fellow of the Fields Institute]] for Research in the Mathematical Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-09-30 |title=Fields Institute Fellows |url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/honours-and-fellowships/fields-institute-fellows |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences |language=en}}</ref> further recognizing his impact in the academic community. Davison's research has been well funded by [[Mitacs|MITACS]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Improving Financial Health in Canada |url=https://www.mitacs.ca/our-projects/improving-financial-health-in-canada/ |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=Mitacs |language=en-CA}}</ref> [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council|NSERC]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Government of Canada |first=Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada |date=2016-06-28 |title=NSERC - Research Grants Competition - Results by GSC - 2020 |url=http://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/NSERC-CRSNG/FundingDecisions-DecisionsFinancement/ResearchGrants-SubventionsDeRecherche/ResultsGSCDetail-ResultatsCSSDetails_eng.asp?Year=2020&GSC=1509 |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC)}}</ref> and private sector partners throughout his academic career.

Davison was Chair of the Department of Statistical & Actuarial Sciences from 2014 to 2017 and Acting Chair of the Applied Math Department from 2015 - 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty - CFIRM - Western University |url=https://cfirm.uwo.ca/people/faculty.html |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=cfirm.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> From 2017 to 2018, he served as the founding director of Western's School of Mathematical & Statistical Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web |title=School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences - Western University |url=https://www.uwo.ca/smss%20/index.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> which was designed to enhance collaborative research and education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences |url=http://www.uwo.ca/sci/undergraduate/future_students/academic_programs/the_school_of_mathematical_and_statistical_sciences.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> That same year, he was appointed Dean of the Faculty of Science,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Matt Davison named next Dean of Western's Faculty of Science |url=http://www.uwo.ca/sci/about_science/media/press_releases/archive/2018/matt_davison_named_next_dean_of_westerns_faculty_of_science.html |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=www.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref> a role he continues to fulfill.<ref name=":0" />

In addition to his university duties, Davison has served the broader academic community. His roles included President of The Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematics Society<ref>{{Cite web |title=CAIMS – The Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematics Society |url=https://caims.ca/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=CAIMS |language=en-US}}</ref> from 2017 to 2019<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Presidents |url=https://caims.ca/past-presidents/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=caims.ca |language=en-US}}</ref> and a board member of the [[Fields Institute]] for Research in the Mathematical Sciences from 2018 to 2021 <ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-12-24 |title=Annual Reports and Newsletters |url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/about/annual_reports |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences |language=en}}</ref> and of the Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction<ref>{{Cite web |last=ICLR |title=Home |url=https://www.iclr.org/ |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=ICLR |language=en-US}}</ref> since 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ICLR |title=About Us |url=https://www.iclr.org/about-us/ |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=ICLR |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, Davison co-founded Canada's Financial Wellness lab,<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Canada's Financial Wellness Lab {{!}} Academic Research on Financial Wellness |url=https://www.financialwellnesslab.ca/ |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=Canada's FWL |language=en}}</ref> which he now leads. This multi-university,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Academic Partners {{!}} Canada's Financial Wellness Lab |url=https://www.financialwellnesslab.ca/academic-partners |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Canada's FWL |language=en}}</ref> multi-stakeholder<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Industry Partners {{!}} Canada's Financial Wellness Lab |url=https://www.financialwellnesslab.ca/industry-partners |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Canada's FWL |language=en}}</ref> initiative focuses on developing quantitative finance and data analytics solutions that will enable Canadian households to enhance their financial resilience.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research {{!}} Canada's Financial Wellness Lab |url=https://www.financialwellnesslab.ca/research |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=Canada's FWL |language=en}}</ref> The lab is a collaboration of several universities,<ref name=":3" /> including [[Wilfrid Laurier University]], [[York University]], the [[University of British Columbia Okanagan|University of British Columbia]], and the [[University of Winnipeg]], along with industry partners<ref name=":4" /> including [[Coast Capital Savings|Coast Capital]], [[Libro Credit Union]], [[Canadian Payroll Association|National Payroll Institute]], [[Ceridian]], [[CI Financial|Aligned Capital Partners (CI Financial)]], and [[Environics Analytics]], to broaden its impact and reach.
